2025 Mastio LTL Carrier Rankings: Insights into Customer Value and Loyalty

  • Kelsea Ansfield
  • Oct 8, 2025
  • 4 min read

At Gain Consulting, we specialize in navigating the intricacies of supply chain logistics, helping businesses optimize carrier selection and reduce costs in an ever-evolving market. The recently released 21st Edition of Mastio's U.S. LTL Carrier Customer Value & Loyalty Report for 2025 provides invaluable insights based on feedback from 1,630 shippers, yielding over 5,100 observations and 5,000 qualitative responses.


Conducted via telephone interviews from late June to late September 2025, this study evaluates 147 carriers, with 24 qualifying for detailed rankings based on a minimum of 30 ratings. Here's a deep dive into the key findings, regional breakdowns, and how these rankings can inform your LTL strategy.


Overview of the Mastio Report

Mastio's annual report delves into the factors driving shipper decisions in the Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) sector. It addresses critical questions such as what influences carrier choice, how value is perceived, competitive standings, customer retention risks, improvement opportunities, and effective marketing strategies. With over 35 years of experience, Mastio delivers unbiased data to help carriers and shippers refine their approaches, mitigate biases, and turn research into actionable outcomes.


The rankings are determined by an Overall Weighted Quality Score, focusing on Customer Value Weighted Performance (Benefit) Scores. Only carriers meeting the 30-rating threshold are included in the primary lists.

Implications for Shippers and the LTL Industry

These rankings reveal a competitive landscape where customer loyalty hinges on value perception, reliability, and service quality. Top performers like Daylight Transport and Old Dominion demonstrate strength in building lasting relationships, while lower-ranked carriers may need to focus on improvements to avoid customer churn. In a market influenced by economic shifts, tariffs, and supply chain disruptions, selecting the right LTL carrier can significantly impact costs and efficiency.


Shippers should consider regional strengths when optimizing routes—for instance, leveraging Pitt Ohio in the Northeast or Southeastern Freight Lines in the South. The qualitative insights from 5,000 responses highlight areas like pricing, on-time delivery, and customer service as key differentiators.
